articleBody:
Before converting an attached garage into an in-law suite, home office, or extra bedroom, running through a detailed checklist keeps unexpected delays and surprise expenses off your plate.

- [ ] Property survey and plot plan — Confirms exterior setbacks and verifies that enclosed additions do not cross zoning boundaries.
- [ ] Local parking regulation check — Ensures your municipality allows converting required covered vehicular parking spaces into habitable rooms.
- [ ] Concrete slab moisture test — Verifies whether moisture rises through the uninsulated slab so proper sealers or subflooring can be specified.
- [ ] Ceiling height measurement — Confirms the clearance from finished slab to framing meets minimal habitable ceiling requirements.
- [ ] Emergency escape window sizing — Guarantees window openings are large enough to satisfy bedroom emergency egress standards.
- [ ] Fire separation assessment — Checks whether walls shared with utility spaces or remaining storage preserve required drywall fire barriers.
- [ ] HVAC and airflow evaluation — Determines if your central system can handle extra square footage or if a ductless split unit is required.
- [ ] Electrical panel capacity audit — Verifies that the breaker box has enough amperage for new lighting, outlets, and dedicated circuits.
- [ ] Plumbing drain line mapping — Locates existing waste stacks if your conversion plan includes adding a bathroom or wet bar.

How to Use This Checklist
Walk through your garage with these items in hand before drawing final floorplans. Addressing these technical factors early prevents costly design changes once construction starts.
